zh.title: 美國陸軍申報以MH-47G直升機使用沖繩下地島機場加油，沖繩縣要求自制
zh.summary: 日本媒體報導，美國陸軍向沖繩縣申報，11月23日下午以兩架 MH-47G 直升機使用宮古島市下地島機場加油。該機場原則上僅供民航機使用，沖繩縣與宮古島市已要求美方自制。
body: 《沖繩時報》等日本媒體報導，美國陸軍在日期為11月16日的文件中向沖繩縣申報，將於11月23日使用宮古島市的下地島機場，目的為加油。依《沖繩時報》報導，申報時段為日本時間下午4時30分至5時30分，使用的是兩架 MH-47G 直升機。琉球朝日放送報導，這兩架直升機據信隸屬日本境外的美軍基地。
下地島機場由沖繩縣管理。沖繩電視臺報導，依1971年琉球政府與日本政府簽署的「屋良覺書」及1979年的「西銘確認書」，該機場原則上僅供民航機使用。《沖繩時報》指出，若美軍依申報使用，將是扣除緊急降落後，自2006年以來、相隔20年的首次。
沖繩縣已向美國陸軍及日美相關機關要求自制。琉球朝日放送報導，縣方在要求中表示「平時應避免經常性使用民用機場」。《宮古新報》報導，宮古島市長嘉數登也發表意見，表示對民航以外的使用，除緊急情況外要求自制的立場不變。
《沖繩時報》11月23日的社論另指出，直升機自菲律賓飛來，加油後將前往嘉手納基地；美軍原先申報使用宮古機場，因無法在希望的時段使用而改為下地島機場。該報並引述沖繩縣知事古謝玄太表示，顧慮對縣民生活、事業活動的影響及心理負擔，美方應避免使用。
沖繩電視臺與《宮古新報》報導，美國海軍陸戰隊2023年也曾以訓練為由申報使用下地島機場，後來未使用。

en.title: US Army files to refuel two MH-47G helicopters at Okinawa's Shimojishima Airport (SHI); prefecture asks it to refrain
en.summary: Japanese media report that the US Army notified Okinawa Prefecture it would use Shimojishima Airport in Miyakojima on the afternoon of November 23 to refuel two MH-47G helicopters. The airport is in principle reserved for civil aircraft, and the prefecture and Miyakojima City have asked the US side to refrain.
body: The US Army notified Okinawa Prefecture, in a filing dated November 16, that it would use Shimojishima Airport (SHI) in Miyakojima on November 23 for refuelling, the Okinawa Times and other Japanese media reported. According to the Okinawa Times, the filing covers 4:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. Japan time and two MH-47G helicopters. Ryukyu Asahi Broadcasting reported that the helicopters are believed to belong to a US base outside Japan.

Shimojishima Airport is managed by Okinawa Prefecture. Okinawa Television reported that under the 1971 Yara memorandum between the then Ryukyu government and the Japanese government, and the 1979 Nishime confirmation, the airport is in principle used only by civil aircraft. If the use goes ahead as filed, it would be the first by the US military since 2006, excluding emergency landings, the Okinawa Times said.

The prefecture has asked the US Army and Japanese and US authorities to refrain. Ryukyu Asahi Broadcasting reported that the request said routine use of civil airports in peacetime should be avoided. Miyakojima Mayor Noboru Kakazu also issued a comment saying the city's position of asking for restraint on non-civil use, except in emergencies, has not changed, the Miyako Shinpo reported.

An Okinawa Times editorial on November 23 added that the helicopters were flying in from the Philippines and would continue to Kadena Air Base after refuelling, and that the US military had first filed to use Miyako Airport (MMY) before switching to Shimojishima when its preferred time slot was unavailable. It quoted Okinawa Governor Genta Koja as saying the US side should refrain because of concern about the effect on residents' lives and business activity and the psychological burden.
Okinawa Television and the Miyako Shinpo reported that the US Marine Corps also filed to use Shimojishima Airport for training in 2023 and did not go ahead.

The filing covers 4:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on November 23 and two MH-47G helicopters.
The helicopters are believed to belong to a US base outside Japan, and the prefecture's request said routine peacetime use of civil airports should be avoided.

The 1971 Yara memorandum and the 1979 Nishime confirmation provide that the airport is in principle used only by civil aircraft; the US Marine Corps filed to use it for training in 2023 and did not go ahead.
Miyakojima Mayor Noboru Kakazu said the city's position of asking for restraint on non-civil use except in emergencies has not changed.
